newsitem.title: UK: IPE BRENT FALLS ON GREEN LIGHT FOR IRAQ OIL SALES.
newsitem.headline: IPE BRENT FALLS ON GREEN LIGHT FOR IRAQ OIL SALES.

text.p: IPE Brent crude fell to new lows after Iraq was given the green light to resume selling oil by the United Nations.
September Brent was down 25 cents at $18.65 a barrel at 1541 GMT after dipping to a fresh intra-day low of $18.56 soon after the news.
"The news about Iraq certainly hit the market but there was a slight delay," said a broker.
The United Nations formally approved Iraq's oil pricing formula after no objections were raied by the UN sanctions committee by the 1500 GMT deadline.
Iraq is now free to sell oil for the first time since the end of May.
The underlying Brent cargo market was also weak despite good rfining margins on both sides of the Atlantic.
Prompt cargoes were pegged some 23 cents under September and some dealers expected the market to move into deeper contango.
Oil products were also weak in Europe. A sharp drop in gasoline helped undermine Brent and IPE gas oil was also trading lower.
August was down $2.75 a tonne at $169.75 with the next technical support around $165.
Dealers said there was good demand for diesel into France but German demand was muted with many traders away from the office on holiday.
The crack spread between gas oil and Brent was also under pressure with swaps easing about 10 or 15 cents to $4.55 a barrel for the winter months.
Despite the bearish tone on futures some dealers saw the chance of stability if refinery margins remain good.
